guard_streams.source: Ofcom new mobile messaging scam rules

facts.detail: Ofcom published the final mobile-messaging scam protection package on 15 July 2026.
Ofcom cited fraud as about 45% of reported crime incidents in England and Wales.
Ofcom cited £1.28 billion lost to criminals in 2025.
Four in ten UK mobile users reported at least one suspicious mobile message in the previous three months.

guard_streams.write_limit: National scam prevalence and losses are not parcel network evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new mobile messaging scam rules

facts.detail: Mobile providers must collect scam-message, link and number information from customers and anti-fraud organisations.
Providers must block numbers used by scammers and stop messages being sent from them.
Providers must identify and block scam messages in transit using malicious links and phone numbers.
Providers must set messaging-volume limits for pay-as-you-go SIM cards.

guard_streams.write_limit: Messaging controls do not prove parcel coverage, speed or availability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new mobile messaging scam rules

facts.detail: Rules cover mobile operators and aggregators transmitting business messages.
New business-message senders require upfront and ongoing Know Your Customer checks.
Providers must review account activity and investigate fraud reports under Know Your Traffic controls.
The controls are intended to stop criminals gaining or retaining access to business messaging services.

guard_streams.write_limit: Business-messaging due diligence is provider-control evidence, not parcel service evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new mobile messaging scam rules

facts.detail: Providers must corroborate alphanumeric sender IDs against information held about the business.
Providers must maintain policies for protected and generic sender IDs.
Incident-management processes must identify criminal activity and accountability failures.
Providers must act on reports to block malicious sender IDs, links and phone numbers.

guard_streams.write_limit: Sender-ID controls cannot identify fixed-network availability at a parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new mobile messaging scam rules

facts.detail: Providers should withhold caller ID for calls appearing to use a UK mobile number while roaming abroad unless validity is verified.
Consumers can report scam messages and mobile calls to 7726.
Mobile providers use 7726 reports to monitor scams and update network protections.
Industry tools were estimated to block more than 600 million scam messages annually.

guard_streams.write_limit: Call and message blocking statistics do not establish parcel coverage or uptime.

facts.detail: Consumers should not reply, click links, press buttons or share personal details when contact is suspicious.
Unexpected contact, urgency and suspicious links are warning signs requiring independent checks.
Suspicious texts should be forwarded to 7726.
Scam calls can be reported to Report Fraud, or Police Scotland in Scotland.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer safety guidance is not broadband availability evidence.

facts.detail: Consumers should hang up when a call may be fraudulent.
Consumers should avoid returning unrecognised calls, especially specified high-cost number ranges.
The suspicious calling number can be forwarded to 7726 free of charge.
Device or provider spam warnings can help but are not always accurate.

guard_streams.write_limit: Call-handling advice cannot populate postcode-level network fields.

facts.detail: An outgoing call displaying a number reserved for inbound use is not a genuine call from that organisation.
Ofcom and UK Finance established the DNO list in 2019.
The list is shared with telecoms providers, intermediaries and some call-filtering services.
DNO inclusion does not guarantee every spoofed call is blocked and not all providers apply the list.

guard_streams.write_limit: DNO protection is unrelated to parcel broadband coverage.
